english.title: Remand prisoner awaiting trial breaking prison
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a prisoner in His Majesty's prison at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..) awaiting trial, broke the said prison by **(..SPECIFY THE METHOD OF ESCAPE..) and by means whereof you escaped
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
prisoner in prison awaiting trial
broke prison and escaped

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See also the associated offence wording as follows: H615 - relating to the offence where sentenced prisoners break prison.
(ii) There must have been an actual breaking eg cutting iron bars. Merely getting over the wall or passing out through a door is an escape (see offence wording H614) and not a breach of prison.
(iii) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.
